title: COMMENTARY: Five charts sounding the alarm for stretched US markets: McGeever
source_used: Reuters commentary (text read on Livemint, Reuters feed)
key_facts: Reuters columnist McGeever writes that US stocks and bonds look highly stretched on several key measures and asks whether an inflection point is near.
Tech and AI stocks make up over 40% of the S&P 500's market value, more than at the peak of the dotcom bubble in early 2000; including AI-related companies the tech share tops 50%, a record.
The equal-weighted S&P 500 is lagging the market-value-weighted index by the widest margin in 24 years.
The equity risk premium (what stocks pay over safe bonds) is at its lowest in 24 years and negative.
The yield on 30-year inflation-protected Treasuries is near 3.40%, the highest since 2002.
The 'term premium' (extra pay for holding long-dated Treasuries) is rising sharply.
The column adds that strong AI profits and healthy growth could still keep the rally going for months or years.
quote_evidence: Tech and AI stocks now comprise over 40% of the S&P 500's market cap.
US stocks and bonds currently appear highly stretched on several key measures, suggesting investors should tread with extreme caution.
why_it_matters_hint: A set of market measures suggests US shares are unusually dependent on tech and AI.
